outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Memory chips, led by Micron flirting with the $1,000 mark alongside SK Hynix and SanDisk
strongest.reason: the memory-chip rebound extended into Monday's pre-market, with Micron nearing a milestone price level as investors continue rotating back into AI-memory names after the July selloff

strongest.area: AI infrastructure capex, driven by hyperscaler spending and fresh institutional buying
strongest.reason: reports that Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft are set to spend close to $600 billion combined on AI infrastructure, plus Berkshire Hathaway's 83% increase to its Alphabet stake, underscore continued conviction in the buildout even as individual stocks were mixed to lower Friday

weakest.area: Enterprise AI software, led by Salesforce, ServiceNow, Adobe, and Palantir
weakest.reason: all four fell 2-3% again Friday, extending a months-long pattern where even fresh analyst price-target increases (Wells Fargo, JPMorgan, UBS) haven't stopped selling tied to fears that AI agents will erode subscription pricing power

Broadcom fell nearly 6% after reports that hackers are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in its VMware vCenter software, a fresh and specific risk distinct from the broader AI-chip-sector volatility

outlook.nextStep: The Broadcom VMware vulnerability is worth a closer look for whether it's a contained, one-time headline risk or a sign of broader exposure, since it's a different kind of risk than the usual AI-capex-sentiment swings. The renewed round of analyst price-target hikes across enterprise software (Salesforce, ServiceNow, CrowdStrike, Zscaler) is probably better watched for confirmation in the stocks themselves over the next few sessions than acted on now, given how persistent the selling has been despite the more optimistic commentary.

signals.title: 10-year yield ticks back toward 4.7% ahead of a quiet pre-Fed week
signals.body: The 10-year Treasury yield eased to around 4.69% Monday morning after edging up roughly 5 basis points in the prior session, with markets still digesting last week's cooler-than-expected July CPI print (3.4% headline, 2.5% core) as they look ahead to the September Fed meeting.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether upcoming data continues to support a September hold, since that's the current market expectation

signals.title: Memory-chip rally extends, with Micron nearing $1,000 premarket
signals.body: Micron shares were flirting with the $1,000 level in Monday premarket trading, with SK Hynix and SanDisk also gaining as investors continue to rotate back into memory names after the July selloff. BofA reiterated Micron as a top pick, and New Street's recent upgrade cited a potential path to a multi-trillion-dollar market cap by 2030.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether this rebound has more room to run or is starting to price in a lot of good news already

signals.title: Broadcom drops nearly 6% on actively exploited VMware vCenter vulnerability
signals.body: Broadcom shares fell sharply Friday after security researchers confirmed hackers are actively exploiting a critical flaw in its VMware vCenter software. This is a distinct, company-specific risk separate from the broader AI-chip-sector swings that have driven most of the recent volatility in chip-adjacent names.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at how quickly the vulnerability gets patched and whether it has any spillover into Broadcom's enterprise software relationships

signals.title: Hyperscaler capex commitments and Berkshire's Alphabet stake highlight continued AI infrastructure conviction
signals.body: A fresh report estimates Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft will spend close to $600 billion combined on AI infrastructure capex, while Berkshire Hathaway disclosed an 83% increase to its Alphabet stake, making it Berkshire's third-largest holding. Both underscore continued institutional and corporate conviction in the AI buildout even as individual megacap stocks were mixed to lower Friday.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at which infrastructure suppliers and cloud providers are best positioned to capture this spending, independent of daily price swings

signals.title: Enterprise software selloff continues despite a fresh wave of analyst price-target hikes
signals.body: Salesforce, ServiceNow, Adobe, and Palantir all fell 2-3% again Friday, extending a pattern seen through the year where even upbeat analyst commentary hasn't stopped the selling. Wells Fargo, JPMorgan, and UBS all raised price targets on software names this week, with JPMorgan explicitly calling AI-disruption fears "overblown," but the stocks have yet to respond.
signals.focus: lower conviction right now given how persistent the selling pressure has been despite the increasingly bullish analyst commentary

signals.title: Cybersecurity names pull back from highs, but analysts raise targets ahead of earnings
signals.body: CrowdStrike and Zscaler both eased further from last week's Black Hat-driven record highs, but a cluster of analysts (Wells Fargo, TD Cowen, RBC, Oppenheimer, Citizens) raised price targets on both names ahead of their upcoming quarterly reports, citing AI-driven cybersecurity spending. Separately, reports of a wave of hacking attacks targeting Wall Street firms and hedge funds underscore the elevated-threat backdrop driving sector demand.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether the pullback is routine profit-taking or the start of a broader cooling, given how sharply the group had run up into earnings season

signals.title: Ouster jumps on Q2 beat and new lidar contract, while Teradyne extends its AI-test-equipment run
signals.body: Ouster shares jumped nearly 8% Friday after a Q2 revenue beat and a new multimillion-dollar Utah traffic-lidar contract expansion, continuing its recovery from earlier-year lows. Teradyne also extended gains, benefiting from continued AI- and robotics-driven demand for its semiconductor test equipment.
signals.focus: worth treating both as still-early, higher-volatility names within the broader robotics theme rather than a read on the sector as a whole
